rows.question: Q1a
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: showed that {rollNo} and {email} are both candidate keys and that {rollNo, name} is a superkey but not a minimal one.

rows.question: Q1b
rows.rubricFeedback: Mapped Advises into Student as an advisorId column, which is only valid if every student has exactly one advisor, and never stated that cardinality assumption.

rows.question: Q2a
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: π name(σ courseId = 'CS F212'(Student ⋈ Enrolment)) returns exactly the names of the students enrolled in CS F212.

rows.question: Q2b
rows.rubricFeedback: Pushed σ dept = 'CS' below the join correctly but gave only the final tree, without the equivalence rule behind each rewrite, so the justification mark was withheld.

rows.question: Q3a
rows.rubricFeedback: Derived A → D correctly but cited transitivity only once, although getting there from A → B, B → C and C → D takes two transitivity steps, so the second justification mark was withheld.

rows.question: Q3b
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: computed {B}+ = {B, C, D} and showed the order in which B → C and C → D were applied.

rows.question: Q3c
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: found all four candidate keys AE, BE, CE and DE and used closures to show that none of them contains a smaller key.

rows.question: Q1a
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: named Running → Ready on a timer interrupt, Running → Waiting on an I/O request and Running → Terminated on exit.

rows.question: Q1b
rows.rubricFeedback: Drew all five states and every transition but left the Waiting → Ready arc without its trigger, I/O completion, and the rubric marks each arc's label.

rows.question: Q2a
rows.rubricFeedback: Listed the heap as private to each thread, but the heap and global variables are shared across the process and only the stack, registers and program counter are per-thread.

rows.question: Q2b
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: explained that one blocking call in a many-to-one user-level library stalls every thread of the process and that one-to-one kernel threads avoid it.

rows.question: Q3a
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: listed saving the outgoing registers and program counter to its PCB, choosing the next process and restoring that process's saved state.

rows.question: Q3b
rows.rubricFeedback: Computed 0.5 / 10.5 correctly but reported the bare number 0.048 without saying it is the fraction of CPU time lost to switching.

rows.question: Q3c
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: showed that halving the quantum to 5 ms raises the overhead to 0.5 / 5.5, about 9.1 percent, roughly double.
